Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberFortress Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for queuing questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberFortress's results for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. With me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberFortress had a strong third quarter, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our Fortress One platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: robust performance across our core product lines like cloud security and SASE, meaningful progress on strategic initiatives, expansion in the number of high-value customers generating over $100,000 in ARR, and accelerating platform adoption over legacy point products.

Before I hand over to John for the financial details, let me provide an update on our progress across those strategic initiatives. At CyberFortress, our guiding principle is delivering next-generation cybersecurity via Fortress One, our integrated XDR platform that merges endpoint detection and response, network security, and cloud workload protection into one AI-powered interface. We've advanced significantly this quarter against a backdrop of escalating threats—ransomware incidents up 35% year-over-year according to Chainalysis, a rise in AI-generated phishing resembling tactics from advanced tools, and ongoing supply chain risks highlighted by events like SolarWinds and Log4j.

These efforts align with four core pillars: AI-driven threat intelligence, zero trust architecture expansion, global market penetration, and strategic acquisitions and partnerships. Let's dive in.

On AI-driven threat intelligence, we've intensified investment in our Fortress AI engine, powered by machine learning on more than 10 trillion daily signals, on par with leading platforms in the space. This quarter, our AI behavioral analytics identified 28% more zero-day threats compared to the prior period, maintaining a false positive rate below 0.3% and achieving mean-time-to-respond under five minutes. ARR from these AI-enhanced features climbed 62% year-over-year to $145 million, or 22% of our total ARR. A standout win was with a Fortune 100 financial services company deploying our GenAI Shield against deepfake social engineering. Ahead, Fortress AI 2.0 launches in Q4 with federated learning for GDPR and CCPA compliance, aiming for 40% better predictive blocking.

Zero trust architecture expansion is another highlight. With Gartner noting 80% of enterprises targeting adoption by 2025, our Fortress Edge SASE solution posted net revenue retention of 128%, propelled by upsells from firewall users. We closed 147 deals exceeding $1 million in ACV, including expansions with two top hyperscalers. Platform adoption rose 45% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations surging 78% to $2.1 billion—current RPO now 135% of ARR. We've embedded continuous adaptive risk and trust assessment, cutting lateral movement risks by 65% in MITRE ATT&CK simulations. We're positioned for 30% SASE revenue growth in fiscal 2024.

For global market penetration, we've evolved beyond U.S. dominance—now 52% of revenue—to diversified growth. EMEA revenue soared 71% year-over-year to $210 million, driven by NIS2 compliance; wins include a leading European telco using Fortress One to counter APT28 amid Ukraine-related tensions. APAC exploded 92% to $165 million, led by Japan and Australia, where our predictive DNS security blocked 1.2 billion malicious queries, tapping into the region's 25% higher ransomware rates per Sophos. LatAm grew 55% with a major Brazilian energy firm securing OT/IoT. U.S. federal holds at 18%, with FedRAMP High nearing completion to challenge Prisma Access.

Finally, on acquisitions and partnerships, we completed the $450 million ThreatLynx deal in May, enhancing deception tech integrated with XDR. Synergies exceed expectations: 15% cross-sell into base, adding $32 million to pipeline. Ties with AWS and Azure fueled 40% of cloud wins, and NVIDIA pilots accelerate GPU anomaly detection for quantum readiness per NIST.

Overall, these moves boosted total ARR to $1.8 billion, up 48% year-over-year, with dollar-based NRR at 122%. Free cash flow margins hit 32%, showing leverage. In a $75 billion TAM growing 15% CAGR per IDC—amid hybrid work, 5G, and AI threats—our 95% gross retention and 4.2x net expansion highlight platform stickiness. We're raising fiscal 2024 guidance: ARR to $7.6-$7.8 billion, non-GAAP operating margin to 28-30%.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan highlighted, we delivered a strong quarter. Revenue for the third quarter reached $950 million, representing a 45% increase year-over-year. This was powered by performance across all product lines. Gross margin expanded to 78%, while operating expenses came in at $520 million. Net income was $180 million, or $1.02 per diluted share.

Building on that, let me detail the performance of our key product lines, where demand remains robust amid hybrid work shifts, multi-cloud adoption, and threats like AI phishing and ransomware-as-a-service. Our lineup—Cloud Security, Secure Access Service Edge or SASE, and next-gen Endpoint Detection and Response or EDR—generated $650 million in Q3 revenue, up 52% year-over-year and comprising 68% of total bookings. ARR for these grew 48% to $2.1 billion, with dollar-based net retention over 118%, signaling strong upsells and cross-sells.

Cloud Security led as our top grower at $285 million, up 55% year-over-year and 42% sequentially—outpacing IDC's 28% CAGR forecast through 2027. This stems from our Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform unifying Cloud Workload Protection, Cloud Security Posture Management, and Data Security Posture Management agentlessly. We gained 650 net new customers, including 120 Fortune 1000 names like a leading U.S. financial firm switching from tools similar to Prisma Cloud.

Technically, our AI-driven Runtime Threat Protection uses behavioral anomaly detection to stop 92% of zero-days in Kubernetes and serverless, topping MITRE ATT&CK cloud analytics. APAC fueled 68% of growth from Japan and India digital mandates against state attacks; EMEA saw 30% ACV lifts from GDPR; North America steady at 55%. With $150 million in R&D—including AWS Bedrock and Azure Arc ties—we're gaining from Wiz and Orca as consolidation rises.

SASE delivered $210 million, up 62% year-over-year and 25% of total ARR, atop Gartner's $25 billion market projection by 2027. Our fabric blends Secure Web Gateway, Cloud Access Security Broker, Zero Trust Network Access, and Firewall-as-a-Service, with RPO up 70% to $1.8 billion as customers ditch VPNs.

We added 450 net new SASE customers, ACV up 28% to $1.2 million via Edge-native low-latency across 150 PoPs. A $45 million European telco deal prevented 15 million DLP incidents, beating Zscaler with GenAI UEBA detecting movement 40% faster and 35% TCO cuts per Forrester. EMEA grew 72% on NIS2 and remote work, outpacing Prisma Access; APAC 55% on 5G; U.S. 45% via CISA. Q4 brings Microsoft Entra interoperability and a ZTNA acquisition for Gartner leadership.

EDR/XDR added $155 million, up 42%, with Falcon-like consolidation, 98% MITRE query efficacy, sub-2% churn, and 75% expansion from cloud/SASE buyers.

These lines shine as threats rose 30% per SonicWall 2024, backed by 1,200 patents and $400 million R&D—we see Q4 acceleration with 75% bookings from cloud and SASE.

Shifting to customer expansion, a key indicator is our high-value cohort over $100,000 ARR, representing enterprise bets on Fortress One against ransomware and APTs. We ended Q3 with 528 such customers, up 17% sequentially from 451 and 32% year-over-year from 399. This validates land-and-expand from EDR to AI SOAR and ZTNA.

Regionally: North America at 68% or 359 customers, up 12% quarter-over-quarter, with three top-10 banks on cloud workload protection post-Colonial Pipeline and SEC rules. EMEA hit 112 or 21%, up 38% on GDPR/NIS2—a European telco expanded to exposure management for $250,000 ACV. APAC reached 57 or 11%, up 25%, strong in Japan/Australia sovereign clouds post-Change Healthcare.

NRR for this group is 128% trailing 12 months, beating SaaS peers; expansions drove 42% adds at $175,000 average upsell via GenAI hunting slashing MTTR 65%. Fortress Mesh SASE-XDR unity resonates versus silos, amid AI vulnerabilities per MITRE. Microsoft/AWS co-sells cut cycles 22%.

We guide to 550-575 by year-end, 25-30% growth, with U.S. Cyber Trust Mark tailwinds; 95% retention offsets APAC risks. This fuels $1.2 billion ARR run-rate and 28% free cash flow margins.

Finally, platform adoption versus point products is reshaping our growth. Per IDC, platforms took 28% market share in 2023 from 18% in 2021. Point solutions like standalone EDR or firewalls breed silos; Fortress One converges XDR, SASE, cloud protection, and zero-trust agentlessly, cutting MTTR 70%.

Q3 platform bookings were 68% of new ARR, up from 52% last year and 78% sequentially; platform ARR hit $1.2 billion, +52% year-over-year, +18% quarter-over-quarter. Point ARR at $420 million was flat year-over-year, down 5% as we migrate.

Platforms offer 42% lower TCO per Forrester, 128% NRR, 2.5x upsells at 65% attach for CloudSec WAF or identity detection. Points lag at 98% NRR, 12% churn. DBNER: 142% platform versus 105% points. 85% Fortune 1000 Q3 deals were platform, displacing Prisma at top banks.

Drivers: GenAI hunting on 15+ billion events for 95% zero-day true positives (#1 MITRE enterprise); agentless cloud for Kubernetes/EKS in 48 hours; OpenXDR API with ServiceNow/Splunk/Sentinel for 30% partner deals.

North America 72% platform ARR, +60% via AWS/Azure; EMEA 22% bookings on NIS2, displacing Fortinet; APAC 55% adoption, 15% ARR in telcos/manufacturing; LatAm 8% with Brazil fintech.

We've sunset three point SKUs, allocating $250 million R&D to quantum encryption, autonomous SOAR; DeepShield AI buy adds $100 million synergies. SMB Essentials tier drives 80% adoption.

Guidance: platform ARR $5.5-6 billion FY2025 end, 45-50% growth; points under 20%. Gartner Leader in XDR/SASE with top execution; 75% gross margins fuel 30%+ growth in 13% CAGR market.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Thank you. Instructions for the Q&A session: Please press * then 1 to queue. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Can you expand on the cloud security momentum, particularly APAC growth and how you're differentiating from Wiz?

Johnathan Hale: Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, cloud security was a standout, with that 55% year-over-year growth to $285 million driven by our CNAPP unification. In APAC, which contributed 68% of bookings acceleration, it's about aligning with digital transformations and countering state-sponsored threats in Japan and India. Versus Wiz or Orca, our agentless platform plus AI runtime protection—blocking 92% zero-days per MITRE—plus deep AWS Bedrock integrations give us consolidation edge. Customers like that U.S. financial firm are migrating for the full posture management stack. We're excited for more share gains with that $150 million R&D push.

Operator: Next question from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great results. On the $100K+ ARR customers, how sustainable is the 128% NRR, especially in EMEA?

John Ramirez: Hi Lisa, thanks. That 128% NRR for our 528 high-value customers is durable, driven by expansions—42% of sequential adds from upsells averaging $175,000, like bundling GenAI hunting. In EMEA, now 112 customers up 38% year-over-year, NIS2 and GDPR are tailwinds; the telco expansion to full exposure management shows it. Our Fortress Mesh reduces silos, and 95% gross retention provides buffer. With partner ecosystem shortening cycles, we see continued strength toward our 550-575 year-end guide.

Operator: Next question from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel: Thanks. Johnathan, on strategic initiatives, any update on the NVIDIA pilot and quantum readiness?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Mike—Johnathan asked me to jump in here. The NVIDIA collaboration on GPU-accelerated anomaly detection is progressing well, directly addressing quantum threats per NIST's post-quantum roadmap. It builds on our Fortress AI processing 10 trillion signals daily, and early tests show massive speedups in threat correlation. This ties into our ThreatLynx acquisition synergies, already at 15% cross-sell, and positions us ahead in predictive defenses. More to share as we scale.

Operator: Our next question from Sarah Lopez with Barclays.

Sarah Lopez: Solid execution. John, thoughts on platform mix shift and point product migration timelines?

Johnathan Hale: Sarah, great question. The 68% platform bookings share, driving $1.2 billion ARR up 52%, is our flywheel—85% of Fortune 1000 deals pure platform. We're migrating aggressively: sunsetted three point SKUs, pushing R&D to innovations like quantum pilots. TCO savings of 42% per Forrester, plus 142% DBNER, make it compelling. FY2025 platform ARR guide of $5.5-6 billion shrinks points below 20%, mirroring leader playbooks. Regional traction in APAC at 55% adoption confirms it.

Operator: Thank you. That concludes our Q&A session.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
